title: Nehemiah Bible Quiz - Chapter 5
description: Ten questions on Nehemiah 5: Nehemiah stops the usury among the Jews and refuses the governor's pay.

questions.text: Against whom did a great cry of the people and their wives arise?
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 5:1 says the cry was against their brothers the Jews.

questions.text: Why were some mortgaging their fields, vineyards and houses?
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 5:3 says they did this to get grain because of the famine.

answers.text: To pay for the timber of the wall
To buy weapons for the guards
To get grain because of the famine

questions.text: For what had some borrowed money using their fields and vineyards as collateral?
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 5:4 says they borrowed money for the king's tribute.

questions.text: What did the narrator say to the nobles and rulers?
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 5:7 says, "You exact usury, everyone of his brother."

answers.text: "You have not built your part of the wall"
"You exact usury, everyone of his brother"

questions.text: Besides fields, vineyards, olive groves and houses, what else were they to restore?
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 5:11 says they were to restore the hundredth part of the money, grain, new wine and oil they were charging.

answers.text: The hundredth part they were charging
Half of all their cattle and sheep
The gold vessels of the temple

questions.text: What did the narrator shake out as a sign against anyone who broke the promise?
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 5:13 says, "I shook out my lap," and asked that God shake out every man who did not perform the promise.

questions.text: For how many years had the narrator and his brothers not eaten the bread of the governor?
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 5:14 says from the twentieth to the thirty-second year of Artaxerxes, that is, twelve years.

questions.text: Besides bread and wine, what did the former governors take from the people?
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 5:15 says they took bread and wine plus forty shekels of silver.

questions.text: What was prepared for one day for the narrator?
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 5:18 says one ox and six choice sheep were prepared for one day, and also fowls "for me."

answers.text: One ox and six choice sheep
Fish from the sea of Tyre

questions.text: What does the narrator ask of God at the end of the chapter?
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 5:19 says, "Remember me, my God, for good, all that I have done for this people."

answers.text: To send rain on the land
